definition: The latent diffusion model (LDM) is a diffusion model architecture developed by the CompVis (Computer Vision & Learning) group at LMU Munich.
details: Introduced in 2015, diffusion models (DMs) are trained with the objective of removing successive applications of noise (commonly Gaussian) on training images. The LDM is an improvement on standard DM by performing diffusion modeling in a latent space, and by allowing self-attention and cross-attention conditioning. LDMs are widely used in practical diffusion models. For instance, Stable Diffusion versions 1.1 to 2.1 were based on the LDM architecture.
story: Picture a novelist who has read so much that, given a first line, they cannot help but write the next one. Think of it this way: The latent diffusion model (LDM) is a diffusion model architecture developed by the CompVis (Computer Vision & Learning) group at LMU Munich. And here is the clever part: Introduced in 2015, diffusion models (DMs) are trained with the objective of removing successive applications of noise (commonly Gaussian) on training images. It is prediction pushed forward — each next word, or pixel, guessed from everything that came before it. And that is Latent diffusion model — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.
